items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then I heard Benny Goodman, of course, everyone did, and he was a giant.

ctx.x: And were you growing up hearing a lot of recordings?

A lot of recordings, and in those days the big bands started recording, Ellington and Benny Goodman, and all those people. And the opera was, very you know, naturally, that permeated especially with my granddad, he loved the opera.

items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: I wanted my big band because I idolized Benny Goodman and Artie Shaw.

ctx.x: There wasn’t that much room but if you were at the top of your game, then maybe you could get enough chances to play.

Yeah. And even when things were really fading here for bebop so to speak, or modern jazz, we could go to Europe, and we’re always recognized in Europe. Seventy percent of my income was in Europe for many years. 1950 around that area is when I decided I wanted a big band, but Willard Alexander came to me and said, “I’m putting together a small group for Count Basie because big bands are kind of folding.” Which I didn’t want to believe.
